counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span directly identifying a foreign body or its composition
No raw span showing malignant cells, biopsy, or tissue diagnosis
No raw span for fever, leukocytosis, or an infectious syndrome
decisive_items: choking episode while eating yellowtail fish approximately 11 months prior to presentation
obstruction of the basal segmental bronchus's lumen with edematous formation in the right lower lung
obstructive pneumonia surrounding edematous area in the right lower lung
response.rationale: R5 is the only candidate directly anchored to the bronchoscopic finding of basal segmental bronchial obstruction, with the choking episode and obstructive pneumonia providing a coherent post-obstructive picture. R1 mistakes obstructive pneumonia for aspiration pneumonia, R2 overreads a high-density structure as malignancy without tissue evidence, and R4 relies on nonspecific smoking history and cough.

rejected.why: Choking and obstructive pneumonia are present, but no raw span supports aspiration pneumonia specifically.
High-density structure and obstruction are nonspecific; no raw span shows malignancy or biopsy.
Smoking history and cough/sputum are nonspecific and do not account for the bronchoscopic obstruction.
